text:
maria: Heads-up — after the 2026-03-15 merge (commit 9f3b2a) we see a sustained token/sec drop on hosted prod for short prompts (~28% drop), and p95 generation latency up ~60ms. Queueing delay graphs look like continuous batching is holding tiny batches too long.

aj: seeing it in staging too. tok/sec baseline was ~12k, now ~8.7k during the same traffic slices. KV cache hit rate dropped from 82% -> 64% on the small-prompt workload.

lee: perf CI also flagged a regression in nightly throughput test — test name: ci/throughput/short-prompts — failing with 20-30% lower tokens/sec. I pushed the raw flamegraph to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/2026-03-16/flame-shortprompts.svg

perf-ci: CI failure log: 
```
=== ci/throughput/short-prompts ===
Expected tokens/sec >= 11000, observed 8700
Top callers: scheduler::select_batch_size, runtime::kernel_fallback
Latency p95 increased by 58ms
```

maria: preliminary profile shows a new codepath in scheduler that biases towards 'drain_time' heuristics and occasionally picks smaller target batch sizes; also kernel selection traces show fallback from fast fused-kernel to slower matmul-kernel on many requests. Not sure why kernel fallback is happening — kernel selector appears to think sequences are longer.

sophie: I can bisect. My suspicion: the prefetch/pacing patch landed in the same PR as the kernel-selection heuristics tweak. If the seqlen threshold is flipped it could cause the kernel mapping and batching to diverge.

aj: agree. quick grep shows change in scheduler config: "prefer_kernel_by_seqlen" added in commit 9f3b2a and defaulted to true. There might be a mis-compare so it matches seq_len >= 0 instead of >= 512 in one path.

lee: ran a quick local reproduce with fakerate ~100r/s short prompts and toggling the flag. With prefer_kernel_by_seqlen=false tokens/sec returns to baseline. With it=true fallback count jumps 3x.

maria: can we flip the flag remotely for the canary to see? We should hold the rollout if we confirm impact. @deploy-bot any chance to pause?

deploy-bot: rollout status: production rollout for release/9f3b2a is currently at 45%. Hold requested by maria. Pausing further rollouts... :white_check_mark:

perf-ci: bisect result (automated): first bad commit: 9f3b2a -> scheduler: add prefer_kernel_by_seqlen heuristic.

sophie: manual bisect confirms: commit 9f3b2a changes two codepaths — scheduler.batch_estimator and kernel.selector — one uses inclusive comparison, the other exclusive. Edge-case seq_len==0 (some sharded requests) hit the wrong kernel. I have a tiny repro and patch: change selector comparison to use the same boundary and add an explicit guard for seq_len==0.

sophie: patch snippet:
```
// kernel_selector.cc
if (req.seq_len == 0) return default_kernel;
if (req.seq_len >= config.kernel_seq_threshold) use_preferred_kernel();
else use_fallback_kernel();
```

aj: while patch is tiny, I recommend reverting the release until we ship a test and the guard. We saw customer impact.

maria: +1. Sophie, can you open the revert PR and include an integration test that simulates short-prompt batching + kv-cache skews?

sophie: on it. Will add test that asserts KV cache hit-rate doesn't fall >10% between toggles and a metric check for tokens/sec.

lee: also file an incident ticket so customer success can ping customers on impacted traffic slices. I'll add graphs and the canary slice IDs.

maria: thanks. Postmortem checklist: (1) add unit + integration test around seq_len boundary (2) add perf CI hook to run short-prompts throughput test on every release (3) add a flag to disable prefer_kernel_by_seqlen quickly.

aj: I'll also add an observability metric to track kernel_fallback_count and scheduler_small_batch_ratio so this is alertable.

deploy-bot: rollout paused. Awaiting revert PR or hotfix toggle.

maria: Great — prioritize revert + test. If anyone has quick mitigation other than revert, post here. :eyes:

sophie: created PR #4182 revert + tests, linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4182 (will also add a follow-up patch with corrected heuristic).

lee: LGTM on revert once CI passes. Let's not roll forward this change until the follow-up is validated in staging perf.

maria: thanks team. We'll follow up in next all-hands with perf slides.

aj: small note — why did KV cache hit-rate drop? I think small-batch dwell time increased and we stopped reusing cached prefixes; we should add a microbenchmark for kv-cache hit-rate vs batching delay.

maria: added to TODOs. Good catch. :thumbsup:
